answer.rationale: The two symptoms with hard numbers this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which are the same funnel stage that memory_86 and memory_31 both speak to; a shortened onboarding flow attacks both at once and is the cheapest reversible change. I want memory_86 verified because it is the single memory my intended action leans on hardest and its summary is unusually vague — 'improved completion rates and time-to-value' with no stated sample, duration, or segment, unlike memory_73 which carries 12 reporting weeks and a stable segment definition. If the archived record shows memory_86 was a short-window or single-cohort read, the durability claim weakens and I would fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the larger of the two declines. I want memory_73 verified for the opposite reason: it is the memory most likely to be misapplied under competitive pressure. It is the obvious reflex answer to a competitor's entry pricing, it is quantified persuasively, and discounting is exactly the lever that inflates signups while degrading the revenue quality the primary objective asks me to protect. Its own summary reports signups up 31% against revenue up only 18%, which is the signature of margin erosion and lower-intent accounts, and it says nothing about retention or downstream expansion. Before I let competitive urgency pull the slot toward price, I want to see whether the original record tracked cohort quality past the discount window or only measured top-of-funnel. Downstream value risk is flagged for both the pricing path (permanent price-anchor damage, adverse selection of churn-prone accounts) and, more mildly, for my chosen action: cutting signup fields can reduce qualification signal and route poorly-fit accounts into self-serve, so I will instrument this on retained qualified revenue and 30-day cohort quality rather than on completion rate alone. I am also holding open that none of these memories were consolidated under current competitive conditions; a competitor changing the price-sensitive SMB mix may have shifted who is entering the funnel, which means all inherited effect sizes are upper bounds, not forecasts. Standard experiment rather than broad rollout for that reason. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) and referral_incentive (memory_57) are plausible but address neither declining metric this week.
